subject: Learning Methods
title: Reading Opinion and Persuasion
description: A micro-lesson that makes Reading Opinion and Persuasion usable.

hook.text: She read an op-ed and agreed completely. Then she read the opposing view and agreed with that too. Something was off.

buildup.text: Persuasive writing is designed to convince, not to inform. Rhetorical techniques can bypass critical thinking.

discovery.text: Identify the purpose before reading: is this informing or persuading? Purpose awareness activates your critical filters.

twist.text: The most dangerous persuasion looks like objective reporting. Watch for loaded language, omitted alternatives,.

climax.text: For any persuasive piece, invert it mentally. What would the strongest counterargument be?

punchline.text: Ask 'is this informing or persuading?' before you read a word.

quiz.question: What is the best defense against persuasive writing?
options: Only read sources you already agree with
Identify whether the text aims to inform or persuade before reading
Read as quickly as possible to reduce emotional impact
